title: Rotary Encoder Control
description: Use rotary encoders for precise position and velocity control in robotic systems, integrating with micro-ROS.
objectives: Understand incremental and quadrature encoder operation
Integrate encoder with DC motor control

connections: L298N GND → Supply GND + Pico GND
warnings: NEVER connect external supply directly to Pico (L298N only)
Encoder must have pull-up enabled on A and B pins
Motor requires external supply (minimum 6V for most)

theory.encoder_quadrature: Quadrature encoders generate two signals phase-shifted by 90° (channels A and B). Reading both allows determining direction and counting pulses with 4x resolution (rising/falling edges on both channels).
theory.interrupts: Interrupts (IRQ) allow instant response to encoder pin changes without polling. Pico GPIO IRQ supports edge detection (RISING, FALLING, BOTH).
theory.odometry: Odometry calculates position based on measured movement. With wheel encoder: distance = (pulses / pulses_per_revolution) × wheel_circumference.
theory.velocity: Angular velocity = Δpulses / Δtime. With moving average filter to smooth readings.

steps.title: Connect and Test Encoder
steps.description: Assemble circuit and validate basic readings
details: Connect encoder according to diagram
Configure GPIOs 16 and 17 as INPUT with PULL_UP
Read pin states in loop
Rotate encoder and observe changes in serial terminal
Confirm both channels (A and B) are working

steps.title: Implement Interrupt Reading
details: Create global variable for pulse counter
Configure IRQ on GPIO 16 (channel A) with BOTH edges
In IRQ callback, read A and B states
Determine direction: if A=HIGH and B=LOW → CW, else CCW
Increment/decrement counter according to direction
Test rotating encoder clockwise and counterclockwise

steps.title: Calculate Angular Velocity
details: Store timestamp of last reading
Calculate Δpulses and Δtime at each update
RPM = (Δpulses / pulses_per_revolution) × (60 / Δtime)
Implement moving average filter with 5 samples
Display velocity on terminal or OLED display

steps.title: Integrate with Motor and Control
steps.description: Control motor speed using encoder feedback
details: Connect DC motor via L298N
Implement PWM control on ENA (GPIO 12)
Create control loop: compare desired vs measured velocity
Adjust PWM proportional to error (simple P controller)
Test with different velocity setpoints

steps.title: Publish Odometry to ROS2
steps.description: Integrate with micro-ROS to publish data
details: Configure micro-ROS as in previous practice
Create publisher on /wheel_odometry topic
Use sensor_msgs/JointState or custom message
Publish: position (total pulses), velocity (RPM), timestamp
Visualize in RQT or Rviz2
Record data with ros2 bag for analysis

bipesProject.description: BIPES project with rotary encoder configured using interrupts. Includes velocity calculation and motor control with feedback.

troubleshooting.problem: Encoder counts wrong pulses or skips
solutions: Add 100nF capacitors between each pin and GND (hardware debounce)
Implement software debounce (ignore pulses < 1ms)
Check pull-ups are enabled
Use 1x resolution initially (channel A only) for testing
Rotate encoder slower during tests

troubleshooting.problem: Direction always same regardless of rotation
solutions: Confirm both channels (A and B) are connected
Check direction determination logic
Test reading A and B without IRQ to validate hardware
Swap A and B if needed (depends on encoder)
Add prints inside callback for debugging
Increase moving average buffer size (10-20 samples)
Use fixed update timer (e.g. 100ms) instead of event-based
Implement low-pass filter instead of simple average
Check for timestamp jitter
At low speed, use time-between-pulses counting

troubleshooting.problem: Motor doesn't respond to proportional control
solutions: Confirm PWM is varying (oscilloscope or LED)
Increase proportional gain (Kp) gradually
Check encoder is mechanically coupled to motor
Add dead zone (motor only starts above certain PWM)
Implement full PID if P alone isn't sufficient

challenges.title: Navigable Menu with Encoder
challenges.description: Use rotary encoder to navigate OLED display menu, and integrated button (SW) to select options.

challenges.title: Absolute Position Control
challenges.description: Implement PID control to move motor to specific angular position (e.g. 360°, 720°) and hold, compensating external disturbances.

challenges.description: Use 2 motors with encoders, implement differential kinematics, calculate robot pose (x, y, θ), publish nav_msgs/Odometry to ROS2, and control with teleop_twist_keyboard.
